analysis:
Examined the stop-string scoping change. EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift head 14-32 adds an optional CBv2StopStringScope. When it is set, the matched stop is recomputed through the SDK's StopHoldback, so it reflects the same scoped scan the engine used, then returned via a prefix match on the tail. Unscoped behavior (head 33-58) is unchanged. EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift head 249-250 passes the bridge's stopStringScope into the CBv2Request. Per the docs change (inference.md base/head 1846), only GPT-OSS sets this scope, to the Harmony final message, so stops inside analysis or tool frames no longer end generation. This is a correctness and functional change to consumer-controlled stop handling. It adds no visible plaintext exposure, authorization, attestation or encryption effect (A-001, TB-002, T-008 unaffected), and the engine still enforces output-token limits.

The tail-prefix match at head 30-31 could misreport which sequence matched if scan.text does not end exactly at the stop start (for example, holdback retaining text before the match). That affects reporting only, not security.

The inference.md head units 2425-2954 are documentation context with no security-control claims changed in this batch.

Submodule bumps (libs/mlx 31f550a->72dffa2, libs/mlx-swift 4926d3d->c633d22, libs/mlx-swift-lm aee6ebb->25bcd63) bring in unreviewed SDK code: StopHoldback, CBv2StopStringScope, the CBv2Request field and any other changes, possibly including MLX JIT/Metal kernels (TB-007, T-028, T-010) or KV/prefix-cache code (T-041). Submodule content is outside the supplied evidence and is a coverage limit, not proof of safety. Integration should confirm the SDK diffs do not alter prefix-cache salt/HMAC handling, media decode bounds, or cancellation/lease semantics. It should also check where stopStringScope is defined on EngineV2Bridge (ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope) and that it is derived from the verified artifact type rather than from a request field.
